interest: U.S. and Chinese intelligence on Japanese activities in Latin America.
overview: This file comprises twenty-six pages of the State Department's official List of Papers (docket register and purport sheets) for decimal file 894.20210, indexing documents 26 through 232 from late 1939 through May 1944 on Japanese military, espionage, and propaganda activities in the Western Hemisphere. The records catalog incoming and outgoing communications among U.S. embassies and legations across Latin America, the Department of State, the FBI, the Office of Strategic Services (OSS), the War and Navy Departments, and the Coordinator of Inter-American Affairs. Major subjects include pre-war Japanese commercial and fishing activities, suspected petroleum concessions in Ecuador (Compañía Minera Petrolera del Pacífico), axis diplomatic and clandestine collaboration with Germany and Italy, tungsten purchasing, and post-Pearl Harbor security assessments. Following the outbreak of the Pacific War, the file tracks the investigation and dismantling of Axis espionage operations—notably the multi-national 'JAPSA' ring operating across Brazil, Argentina, Chile, and Colombia—clandestine courier channels, radio intercept monitoring, propaganda campaigns, and the internment and repatriation of Japanese nationals.
